# Changelog

Every published companion build has an entry below. Android packages are laboratory builds; iOS packages require Apple signing and provisioning. Historical validation belongs to the named version and does not establish current physical-device performance.

## [0.2.11](https://github.com/sev7enITA/NodeLift/releases/tag/v0.2.11): build 13 · 2026-11-02

**Model metadata and transparent companion updates** · experimental-prerelease

- Show Hugging Face repository update and creation dates, task, reported parameters, context, license, languages, base models, gated access and popularity when supplied. Missing metadata stays unknown. Repository dates are not original model release dates.
- Show matching release notes before an explicit direct APK or unsigned IPA download. Validate version, build, publication date and artifact metadata; invalidate stale details after failed checks. Current releases can also be reviewed.
- Allow an explicitly confirmed legacy enrollment to be retired into a stable enrollment while retaining assessment and job history. Established identities are never merged by device name or IP address.

**Validation:** 118 host tests, five desktop JavaScript suites, 21 Android JVM tests, Android lint (0 errors, 17 warnings), both Swift policy suites and unsigned iOS ARM64 build passed. Live Hugging Face metadata rendering and one retained legacy/stable enrollment were verified on the local dashboard. Gemini 4 Argon High supplied a textual UX review. Physical device installation, accessibility and browser download handoff remain unqualified.

**Limits:** Android remains debug-signed with the existing laboratory signer. iOS requires Apple signing and provisioning; downloading an IPA cannot install it. Browser downloads are not hash-verified by the companion. No new inference speedup or shared-memory capability is claimed. HarmonyOS/NEXT builds remain deferred.

## [0.2.9](https://github.com/sev7enITA/NodeLift/releases/tag/v0.2.9): build 11 · 2026-11-01

**Device assessment, session visibility and simpler companions** · experimental-prerelease

- Show authenticated peer IP, enrollment dates, latest contact and observed session boundaries for devices; show host LAN address and process session start. Legacy dates remain unknown until observed.
- Automatically schedule bounded sequential network and synthetic CPU assessment for newly enrolled devices, with explicit retry and classifications based on returned measurements. Low battery, severe thermal state and host inference defer automatic work. A changed peer address invalidates the prior connection classification.
- Replace ambiguous contribution labels with explicit host target/verifier role, no selected run, external route, unused phone, missing accounting or measured zero. Basic diagnostics never claim LLM speedup or shared RAM.
- Reorganize Android and iOS into Home, Activity and Settings, separate connection from draft readiness, expose one next action, move advanced controls into disclosure and make diagnostic export directly available. Retain identity confirmation for QR and manual pairing.
- Age the connection indicator from successful authenticated responses so a stale session cannot stay marked active indefinitely. This is status reporting, not a claimed fix for the unresolved physical network timeout.

**Validation:** 115 host tests, five JavaScript suites, 18 Android JVM tests, Android lint (0 errors, 17 warnings) and unsigned iOS ARM64 compilation passed. An isolated browser and synthetic TLS worker exercised enrollment and sequential assessment. Gemini 4 Argon High provided a textual UX architecture review. Physical accessibility, networking and LLM speedup remain unqualified.

**Limits:** Physical Android/iOS accessibility and stable mobile inference are not qualified. Basic assessment is HTTPS plus a synthetic CPU kernel; model-specific usefulness still needs a matched native comparison. Session boundaries are inferred after a contact gap over 20 seconds. iOS packages require Apple signing. HarmonyOS/NEXT remains deferred.

## [0.2.8](https://github.com/sev7enITA/NodeLift/releases/tag/v0.2.8): build 10 · 2026-11-01

**Stable device enrollment and local dashboard recovery** · experimental-prerelease

- Android and iOS store a private installation identity in Android Keystore-encrypted storage or iOS Keychain. Pairing derives a separate key for each host, so scanning another QR reuses the same node and renews its access credential. No IMEI, MAC address or hardware fingerprint is collected.
- Existing enrollment is adopted only after an invitation-bound proof of the saved credential. Different phones with the same model remain separate. Interrupted pairing can recover with a new QR and the persisted identity.
- The desktop offers a protected Restore local session button with localized feedback. Owner-confirmed legacy consolidation preserves diagnostic jobs and their original enrollment IDs.

**Validation:** Android build, 14 JVM tests and lint (0 errors, 17 warnings), unsigned iOS ARM64 build, 10 enrollment identity tests, 24 host protocol/network tests and real Swift TLS repeat enrollment on macOS passed. Kotlin/Swift identity and proof vectors match the host. Physical-phone repeated QR qualification remains pending.

**Limits:** Update the desktop host before pairing with 0.2.8. Removing Android app data or losing identity storage creates a new installation; automatic physical-device recognition after identity loss is not claimed. Older companions do not send identity proof. HarmonyOS/NEXT builds remain deferred. No inference performance claim.

## [0.2.7](https://github.com/sev7enITA/NodeLift/releases/tag/v0.2.7): build 9 · 2026-11-01

**Current-network QR pairing and the approved 3D emblem** · experimental-prerelease

- Use the approved blue three-dimensional showcase emblem in Android/iOS launcher icons and native headers, the GitHub README and HarmonyOS source assets. Keep the simplified mark for small monochrome system surfaces.
- The host follows its current private IPv4 route when creating a pairing QR, validates the local bind and retires stale invitations after a network move. Per-address TLS identities preserve certificate and hostname verification; companions scan a fresh QR after an address change. Enrollment and measurement history remain available.
- Android routes paired-host requests through a matching connected Wi-Fi/Ethernet network when available, retaining system routing for tethering. Network timeouts and TLS identity failures have distinct localized guidance. Exported diagnostics include only allowlisted route events and available transport categories.
- Desktop graph links use color and width for measured accepted draft token share. Selected running draft routes animate; completed, offline, unknown and fallback routes stay still. A motion toggle, background pause and reduced-motion support are included.
- Publish a pinned Locally Uncensored source assessment with attribution and clear boundaries between independently implemented diagnostics and future planner/cancellation requirements.

**Validation:** Android compilation, 13 JVM tests and lint (0 errors, 19 warnings), unsigned iOS ARM64 device build, 24 host protocol/network tests, localization and graph accounting checks passed. Browser fixture verified weighted animation and the motion toggle using explicitly synthetic data. Android signer continuity, packaged artwork, unchanged native LLM libraries and identical ZIP/IPA app payloads were verified. Physical-device reconnection and installation remain unconfirmed.

**Limits:** No physical Oppo/Xiaomi installation or camera qualification in this build. Token share is not compute utilization or a speedup. iOS packages require Apple signing. HarmonyOS/NEXT source artwork is updated but native builds remain deferred. Native LLM libraries are reused; no engine performance claim.

## [0.2.6](https://github.com/sev7enITA/NodeLift/releases/tag/v0.2.6): build 8 · 2026-11-01

**Reliable controls, local diagnostics and automatic update checks** · experimental-prerelease

- Replace the Android legacy scanner activity with lifecycle-bound CameraX, an offline ZXing decoder, retry/cancel controls and a camera-open timeout. Permission denial and camera errors return actionable feedback; invitation validation and identity confirmation remain required.
- Android controls distinguish available, disabled, pressed, selected and busy states. Session status, engine permission and actual draft readiness are separate; saved engine permission is synchronized after service changes.
- Desktop actions show request progress across polling updates and block duplicate submissions. Narrow-screen Add device labels and QR spacing are repaired. iOS controls gain explicit pressed/disabled styling and connection progress.
- English, Simplified Chinese and Italian messages, Android APK and unsigned iOS packages share version 0.2.6/build 8. Native LLM libraries are reused without engine changes.
- Add bounded local Android/iOS diagnostic journals with explicit export and clear, sanitized managed exception context, supported Android process exit reasons and reduced iOS MetricKit events. Previous interruption markers do not establish a crash cause.
- Check official companion release metadata at launch and weekly while running, with due checks after OS suspension, offline retry and an explicit Check now action. Installation remains manual.
- Use the current original orbital NodeLift mark in native headers and launcher icons. Add project acknowledgements and preserve original third-party licenses and source.

**Validation:** Android app/instrumentation compilation and lint, ten JVM QR/support policy tests, unsigned iOS device compilation, Swift journal/update checks, 19 host protocol tests, localization and focused desktop control tests passed. Android signing continuity and unchanged native libraries were verified. Actual external source/design reviews are scoped in release evidence. Physical scanning, sharing and weekly scheduling on a phone were not tested.

**Limits:** The reported Xiaomi crash remains unconfirmed without a device log; install and exercise the new APK. Logs are best effort and cannot capture every native crash. OS suspension delays checks until execution resumes. iOS packages require Apple signing; TestFlight/App Store distribution is planned, not available. HarmonyOS/NEXT builds remain deferred. No new inference speedup or pooled-RAM result.

## [0.2.5](https://github.com/sev7enITA/NodeLift/releases/tag/v0.2.5): build 7 · 2026-11-01

**Desktop QR pairing and native mobile scanning** · experimental-prerelease

- Add device on the desktop displays an offline QR; Android and iOS companions scan it and request address/fingerprint confirmation. Manual invitation import remains available.
- Five-minute, single-use invitations expire, clear after use and are revoked when explicitly closed. Camera access is requested only for scanning; pairing does not enable inference automatically.
- Android retains the existing debug signer and saved pairings, with an explicit host leaf-certificate pin. Update and restart the desktop host to use the new pairing flow.
- Android ARM64 APK, unsigned iOS IPA/app ZIP and SHA-256 manifests are published. Native engine libraries are unchanged from 0.2.4.

**Validation:** Android and unsigned iOS device compilation, host protocol and desktop lifecycle checks, Swift parsing and loopback TLS tests passed. Independent ZXing decoding recovered the QR from a desktop screenshot. Published package hashes were verified.

**Limits:** Physical Android/iOS camera scanning remains unqualified. iOS requires personal Apple signing/provisioning and cannot install directly from Safari. HarmonyOS/NEXT builds are deferred. No inference speedup or RAM-pooling claim.

## [0.2.1](https://github.com/sev7enITA/NodeLift/releases/tag/v0.2.1): build 3 · 2026-10-31

**Native inference and authenticated mobile draft workers** · experimental-prerelease

- Pinned llama.cpp core, greedy block verification, correction/bonus tokens, KV resynchronization, identity checks, pinned TLS leases and bounded remote fallback.
- Android ARM64 CPU and iOS Metal/CPU workers, model integrity and battery/thermal/lifecycle controls; authenticated text/SSE gateway and LM Studio generator adapter.
- Actual Gemini 4 High and GLM 5.3 Max design/source reviews were adjudicated. The frozen small-pair local-draft block-4 control reached 0.719× host-only speed, with all 48 paired token sequences matching.

**Validation:** 26 host tests, 29 real-weight native checks, four real-weight TLS loopback fault cases, live gateway checks and three adapter stream tests passed. Android and unsigned iOS device builds compiled.

**Limits:** The remote test node was emulated. Physical-phone inference/speedup, sustained thermals, capacity sharding, hybrid speculative checkpoints, HarmonyOS native worker and installed LM Studio GUI qualification remained open. The 27B upstream kernel result is not NodeLift hybrid-model support.

## Host, documentation and tooling updates

### 2026-11-02: Physical iPhone results and private iOS build 0.2.12 (15)

- Complete 18 original iPhone-versus-Mac pairs with matching outputs. Fixed phone delegation at a 32-token budget has a median paired 4.657x slowdown, +1040.652 ms total and +109.299 ms TTFT, with 128/246 proposals accepted. The iPhone route has a smaller observed penalty than the earlier Xiaomi route, but the backend and topology differ.
- Both adaptive cells fall back in every request, with no accepted phone tokens. A signed total-time improvement in one short cell is not phone acceleration. The fixed-128 cell stops after connection drift; retain one invalid and five missing primary attempts.
- Fix iOS handling of obsolete draft-result rejection so expected expired or superseded output is discarded without ending the session. Add a local diagnostic event and regression tests. Sign and install private development build 0.2.12 (15); post-fix physical validation is separate.
- Publish the frozen plan, raw sessions, failure record and descriptive comparison in research/iphone-tradeoffs-2026-11-02/REPORT.md. Energy, sustained thermals, independent confidence intervals and larger-target benefit remain unqualified. Public companion downloads remain 0.2.11 (13).

### 2026-11-02: iOS draft setup: private development build 0.2.12 (14)

- Add the missing iOS download-from-Mac action, progress, cancellation and an explicit development-transfer import action in English, Simplified Chinese and Italian. Setup verifies the paired host hash before enabling proposals; resume the session to load the engine.
- Use pinned authenticated TLS, fixed endpoints, bounded streamed transfer and integrity checks before replacement. Add integration coverage for transfer failure, certificate mismatch and cancellation cleanup.
- Sign and install private iOS build 0.2.12 (14) over 0.2.8 on the owner's physical iPhone. Copy and import the selected draft. Native inference readiness and performance results remain separate from installation and import.
- Public downloads remain 0.2.11 (13). This development installation is not a public, TestFlight or App Store release. See docs/IOS_DRAFT_SETUP.md for setup steps, validation and limitations.

### 2026-11-02: Physical Xiaomi trade-offs: latency loss and adaptive containment

- Run 18 new physical Xiaomi-versus-Mac pairs plus 3 local-draft control pairs with matching outputs. Fixed phone drafting at a 32-token budget showed a median 134.949x slowdown in this model/hotspot scope.
- Adaptive phone probing returned to the host in all 12 adaptive requests. Median paired overhead was 43.738 ms at a 32-token budget and 87.604 ms at 128 tokens; no phone tokens were used. This contains loss and does not demonstrate acceleration.
- Retain policy/width fingerprints, decision blocks and contextual telemetry. Fix the collector clock boundary and show fallback-inclusive completed-service timing separately in Measurements.
- A separate post-hoc network diagnostic timed out without samples. Energy, sustained thermals, larger targets and other phones/transports remain unqualified. Full protocol, raw records and trade-off matrix: research/phone-tradeoffs-2026-11-02/REPORT.md.
- Validation: 138 host tests, seven desktop JavaScript suites, generated localization checks and 95-page documentation validation passed. All saved reports reproduce from raw sessions; fallback-inclusive timing is visible in the live dashboard.
- Host tooling and desktop update only. Native inference engine and companion binaries are unchanged; public Android/iOS packages remain 0.2.11/build 13.

### 2026-11-02: NodeLift Impact v1: scoped time, TTFT, reliability, energy and uncertainty

- Add an explicit paired native SSE collector, local impact-analysis API and Measurements import/export panel in English, Simplified Chinese and Italian. Reports retain fallback, missing and mismatched attempts for one model/device/connection scope.
- Implement whole-session bootstrap uncertainty, full-coverage instrumented-energy integration and explicit qualification gates. Missing energy remains unavailable; effective offload, residency and independent-session attestation remain incomplete, so automatic routing promotion is disabled.
- Methodology reviewed through GLM 5.3 Max and Gemini 4 Argon High. A three-pair Xiaomi hotspot pilot completed with matching outputs, one fallback and no observed speed benefit; one session cannot establish confidence intervals. See docs/IMPACT_BENCHMARK.md and research/impact-2026-11-02/REPORT.md.
- Validation: 136 host tests, seven JavaScript suites, generated localization/release checks and 92-page documentation validation passed. The real dashboard and authenticated analysis endpoint rendered the physical pilot with explicit missing energy and no qualified recommendation.
- Host, analysis and desktop update only. Native engine and Android/iOS binaries remain unchanged at companion 0.2.11/build 13.

### 2026-11-02: Desktop contextual help and explicit engine capability boundaries

- Add contextual explanations beside desktop controls and a browser-local Options preference to disable or restore them. Essential limitations remain visible.
- Document native generation, local and phone drafting, prompt lookup, adaptive control and external text routes separately from unimplemented capacity sharding and unqualified physical-phone speedup. See docs/ENGINE_STATUS.md in the repository.
- Desktop and documentation update only. Android and iOS packages remain 0.2.11/build 13; no new native inference benchmark is claimed.

### 2026-11-02: Execution backend catalog controls and model-selection guidance

- Add catalog loading and matching provider configuration next to Execution backend, with inline errors, empty-catalog guidance and immediate model-selection readiness. Native target/draft controls are disabled for external execution.
- Explain that Main model lists discovered/imported GGUF files, not recommended or certified-compatible models, and that draft models are optional token proposers for drafting strategies.
- Verify actual OpenRouter catalog selection without cloud generation and an end-to-end text response through an existing LM Studio local server. Focused control, model-library, graph and localization suites pass. Host/UI update only; mobile packages remain 0.2.9/build 11.

### 2026-11-01: Host functional QA with GLM and Gemini, fixes and physical-device limits

- Fix cancelled-download error feedback, canonical model provenance and small-model size labels. Localize additional native/validation errors and expose the recorded reason when a run falls back to the computer.
- Execute real browser model upload, cancellation, native run/stop/reconfiguration, gateway and localization checks with GLM 5.3 Max and Gemini 4 High providing mediated test plans and reviews. Publish a scoped audit and sanitized receipts; external models did not operate localhost.
- A physical Xiaomi completed draft loading and CPU calibration, but two network jobs timed out and no stable remote inference route was qualified. Preserve these failures and the unresolved legacy enrollment duplication. No mobile speedup or pooled RAM claim; companion binaries remain 0.2.8.

Verify a 16-token native Qwen run and the live public OpenRouter catalog. - Repository guides, historical assessments and research dossiers are maintained in English; application/showcase localization remains English, Simplified Chinese and Italian.

Publication dates are UTC. Companion versions and the host preview version are separate. Original published binaries and tags are not rewritten for documentation corrections.
